summary_1line: King Sivi sacrifices his own flesh to save a pigeon from a hawk, proving perfect kingship; Bhishma then teaches Yudhishthira that honoring Brahmanas is a king’s foremost duty.

image_candidates.scene_text: King Sivi, bleeding and skeletal, climbs onto a balance scale to equal the weight of a pigeon while a hawk watches.
Inside the palace, queens rush out weeping as the king cuts flesh from his body before a weighing balance holding the pigeon.
Celestial beings shower flowers and nectar as the wounded King Sivi rises into a radiant golden chariot toward heaven.
